newsitem.title: GREECE: THOUSANDS OF GREEK FARMERS GATHER IN ATHENS.
newsitem.headline: THOUSANDS OF GREEK FARMERS GATHER IN ATHENS.

text.p: Thousands of farmers gathered at Athens' Vathis Square on Thursday before starting a march on parliament to press demands for cheaper fuel prices and higher state subsidies on agricultural products.
Several thousand farmers were in Vathis Square and waiting for scores of buses packed with others before setting out for parliament.
The buses, coming in from Larissa and further north, have halted almost all traffic around Omonia Square. Police appealed on radio and television for people to avoid driving in Athens' centre.
The march was expected to start at around 14:30 local time.
Construction workers and pensioners were expected to join the farmers' march to protest against the economic policies of Prime Minister Costas Simitis.
The farmers have blocked the Athens-Salonika highway with thousands of tractors for 22 days, virtually cutting Greece in two.
They have demanded a meeting with Simitis to discuss their grievances but he has responded with a flat "no" until they lift their blockades.
Several thousand police reinforcements have been called up in Athens to control the march and to prevent the farmers from reaching Simitis's central office at Megaro Maximou.
Riot police were heavy in the area around the presidential palace and the Rigilis area where the prime minister's office is. They have said the protesters will not be allowed through.
The farmers are likely to meet the minister to the prime minister George Paschalides and Argriculture Minister Stephanos Tzoumakas. --Costas Paris, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
